Join our team, and let’s win together while having fun! Let’s put our collective minds together, get creative, and have a great time during the NASA Space Apps Challenge!
summary:
Moonatics is an interactive educational web game for children aged 7-12, created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 - Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer. We have three missions, Life Support, Space Greenhouse, Solar Storm Protocol. 

Kids take responsibility for a lunar outpost and complete three connected missions inspired by real NASA data. Missions include keeping the habitat stable, growing food in space, and protecting the crew during a solar radiation event.

Instead of memorizing facts, players learn by observing systems, making decisions, seeing results, and managing lmited resources.
details:
MOONATICS is an interactive educational web game for children aged 7–12, created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer” challenge. Players operate a lunar outpost through three connected missions: Life Support, Space Greenhouse, and Solar Storm Protocol. Besides learning through quizzes, players can observe systems, make decisions, and see the consequences of those decisions.

The game uses real NASA data as the evidence layer. Mission 1 uses RR-28 environmental telemetry, Mission 2 is inspired by the VEG-05 tomato experiment, and Mission 3 uses DONKI space-weather events and CRaTER-D1D2 radiation measurements. We clearly separate NASA observations from MOONATICS simulation: the real data provides the scenario, while resource costs, gameplay thresholds, shelter effects, and other consequences are calculated by our educational model.

A key creative feature is that the missions are connected. Water, energy, crop health, and other outcomes can carry forward, so earlier decisions affect later options. Each mission also uses a different interaction style: system adjustment in Life Support, plant inspection and care in the greenhouse, and emergency preparation and power prioritization during the solar storm. The game includes Explorer mode for ages 7–9 and Mission Specialist mode for ages 10–12, using the same underlying simulation with different levels of scientific detail and difficulty.

We designed MOONATICS with cognitive load, accessibility, and scientific clarity in mind. Briefings introduce one idea at a time, there are no countdown timers, and players can replay missions and experiment without pressure. The project was built with React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI, Vitest, and React Testing Library, and is deployed through GitHub Pages.

Our intended impact is to help younger learners understand systems thinking, resource trade-offs, space biology, environmental control, space weather, and radiation protection through an engaging decision-based experience.
